PAPER-DIVERGENCE (user-ordered WHY): Kim #5 predicts assembly-specific E-to-I beats global inhibition on overlapping engrams — our INH is still ONE shared MLP (same weights for all 250 slots), i.e. nonlinear GLOBAL inhibition, not separate inhibitory neurons per assembly with heterosynaptic E-to-I plasticity. Shared weights cannot express slot-specific suppression when true/dist encodings overlap (distractors are matched-Gaussian re-seeds of true stats at 8-dim); the optimizer parks INH at a constant and satisfies CE through the linear scorer, ignoring the hinge direction — same failure mode as U25, one level up. To #8/Cohen #9 separable-substrates prediction HOLDS as dissociation (SELECT vs SUMMARY move independently across seeds); the shared pool+hinge couples them in training, which is why joint pressure never moves both. Liu #11 boundary carried (heavily-cued task shrinks state effects; not re-tested).
